To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

nuclear recoil energy is well-reconstructed using the combined (ionization and scintillation) energy scale proposed in Shutt et al., that the quench factor for nuclear recoils is well-described by a simple theory that includes only electronic stopping power and Lindhard's theory of electronic excitation, and that the Thomas-Imele box model describes the partitioning of nuclear recoil energy into scintillation, ionization, and heat.
the scintillation efficiency for nuclear recoils in LXe is well-described by theory and that the scintillaton and ionization signals from nuclear recoils are well-described by the box model.
the quench factor is well-described by theory, and the scintillation fraction is well-described by a simple box model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the energy scale of nuclear recoils in xenon.
the physics of nuclear recoils in xenon, with applications to the direct detection dark matter.
the energy scale in liquid noble gas dark matter experiments, which are based on the observation of nuclear recoils.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nuclear recoil energy scale in LXe is well-described by existing theory.

the quench factor for nuclear recoil in liquid xenon, reconstructed using the scintillation and the ionization signals, is 0.25±0.03, and the quench factor reconstructed using only scintillation is 0.21±0.02.
the nuclear recoil energy scale in LXe has been determined to a precision of 1% and that the quench of electronic excitation in LXe has also been determined to a similar precision.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nuclear recoil energy scale in xenon is better determined by using the combined scintillation and charge scale, rather than using the scintillation scale alone.

the energy scales of nuclear recoils in xenon are well-described by Lindhart theory if the nuclear recoil energies are reconstructed using the combined scintillation and electron recoil energy scales proposed by Shutt.
the nuclear recoil energy scale in LUX and XENON10 has been established to within a few percent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy scale of nuclear recoils in the direct detection of WIMP dark matter can now be determined with high accuracy.
the quench factor is well described by Lindhard theory if the nuclear recoil is reconstructed using the energy scale of Shutt et al.
the nuclear recoil energy scale in a liquid xenon target can be determined from the Lindhard theory of electron excitation by fast ions.
